correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 full-dimensional and signed-symmetric K_n has all 4(n-1) sign-edge facets. Uniqueness forces diagonal ellipsoids. John log product with b_i+b_(i+1)<=1 is solved by disjoint AM–GM (even) or explicit positive KKT multipliers lambda_(2k-1)=n(m+1-k)/(m(m+1)), lambda_(2k)=nk/(m(m+1)) (odd). Löwner log product with every independent-set bound is solved by parity-class AM–GM, and the resulting precision c_i=(n b_i)^(-1). All equality cases, contact counts, balls and volume limits follow symbolically. Standalone exact checker n=3..16 and numerical log-det programs n=3..11 passed; finite checks are corroborative. Risk: generality limited to standard Euclidean metric, no independent proof audit.

A general graph-entropy theorem may implicitly subsume some parts; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The alternating fence is a canonical infinite nonlayered height-two family. Sharp odd-fence John optimality extends a previously attained entropy bound beyond its published layered families. The dual Löwner optimizer has a parity contact transition (m+1 supports at n=2m but only two supports at n=2m+1); the odd ellipsoid retains a finite e^(-1/2) volume advantage over its round enclosing ball despite tending to isotropic semiaxes. These are motivated, exact, all-dimension Euclidean invariants, not routine equality checking or finite table recomputation. Risk: long-established entropy duality could make portions accessible to specialists.
